questions.q: Where does Branson look for new business opportunities?
a: Industries where customers have long been badly treated
Markets where a rival has already built perfect service
Sectors that governments are about to regulate heavily
Niche areas that no large company has noticed yet
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the worse and longer the bad experience, the bigger the opening.

questions.q: What was Branson's approach when starting the Elders charity?
a: Gather outstanding people first and define the focus later
Write a detailed strategy before recruiting anyone at all
Raise money first and let donors choose the causes
Wait for a single clear mission to emerge on its own
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Virgin Unite had no theme until the team was already assembled.

questions.q: Why did Branson partner with NTL despite its poor customer service?
a: Its infrastructure could reach many homes quickly, and service could be fixed
It had the best reputation for support in the telecom industry
Regulators required Virgin to work with an established carrier
It was the only company willing to lend him the money
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the deal gave Virgin fast access, and he replaced the call scripts.

questions.q: Why did Branson launch Virgin Atlantic?
a: British Airways offered poor food, entertainment and service
The British government asked him to rescue a failing airline
He had already built a large fleet for another business
Air travel was completely unregulated at the time
questions.why: Lesson 1 presents the airline as a response to a miserable customer experience.

questions.q: What question does Branson start every new venture with?
a: How can I make this fun for everyone involved?
How much money can this generate in year one?
Which competitor can we buy out first?
What is the fastest way to scale this globally?
questions.why: The overview says he approaches business from a position of play and enjoyment.
